name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
description: Fifth-century rock fortress with frescoes, mirror wall and water gardens; a steep climb to the summit palace ruins with panoramic views. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Pidurangala Rock
description: Rock next to Sigiriya with a cave temple and a reclining Buddha; a short scramble to the top gives the best sunrise view of Sigiriya.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
description: Five cave shrines filled with Buddha statues and painted ceilings dating back over 2,000 years. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Polonnaruwa Ancient City
description: Medieval royal capital with palaces, the Gal Vihara rock-cut Buddhas and well-preserved stupas, best explored by bicycle. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Anuradhapura Sacred City
description: Ancient first capital of Sri Lanka with giant dagobas, monasteries and royal ruins spread over a large area. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Sri Maha Bodhi
description: Sacred fig tree grown from a cutting of the Bodhi tree in India, one of the holiest Buddhist sites in the world; busy on Poya days.

name: Ruwanwelisaya
description: Huge white stupa built by King Dutugemunu, surrounded by a wall of elephant sculptures; beautiful in the evening.

name: Jetavanaramaya
description: One of the tallest brick structures of the ancient world, a massive red-brick stupa with monastery ruins around it.

name: Isurumuniya Temple
description: Rock temple beside a pond, known for the 'Isurumuniya Lovers' stone carving and elephant reliefs.

name: Mihintale
description: Mountain where Buddhism was introduced to Sri Lanka; climb 1,840 granite steps to stupas and a rock with wide views. Very busy in June (Poson).

name: Minneriya National Park
description: Jeep safari park famous for 'The Gathering', when hundreds of wild elephants come to the reservoir in the dry season.

name: Kaudulla National Park
description: Less crowded alternative to Minneriya with large elephant herds around Kaudulla tank; good safari value.

name: Hurulu Eco Park
description: Quiet biosphere reserve near Habarana, often used for elephant safaris when Minneriya and Kaudulla are out of season.

name: Wasgamuwa National Park
description: Remote, uncrowded national park with elephants, sloth bears and birdlife along the Mahaweli river.

name: Ritigala Forest Monastery
description: Ancient forest monastery ruins in a jungle-covered mountain reserve; peaceful paths and stone meditation platforms.

name: Aukana Buddha Statue
description: Twelve-metre standing Buddha carved from a single granite rock face in the 5th century.

name: Kalawewa Reservoir
description: Ancient reservoir built by King Dhatusena; calm lakeside views, birdlife and occasional wild elephants.

name: Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
description: 13th-century rock capital with an ornate stone staircase and a lion carving; a quiet alternative to Sigiriya.

name: Nalanda Gedige
description: Stone temple in a mixed Hindu-Buddhist architectural style, standing alone beside a reservoir.

name: Aluvihare Rock Temple
description: Cave temple where the Buddhist Pali Canon was first written down on palm leaves; includes a small manuscript museum.

name: Sri Muthumariamman Temple
description: Hindu temple with a tall, brightly painted gopuram tower covered in deity sculptures.

name: Matale Spice Gardens
description: Guided walks through cinnamon, pepper and cardamom gardens with spice tasting and herbal products; some offer cooking demos.

name: Hiriwadunna Village Tour
description: Rural experience near Habarana: bullock cart and catamaran ride, then a traditional Sri Lankan lunch cooked in a village home.

name: Popham's Arboretum
description: Dry-zone forest arboretum with walking trails, birds and native trees near Dambulla.

name: Ibbankatuwa Megalithic Tombs
description: Prehistoric burial site around 2,700 years old with stone cist tombs and a small museum.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
description: Royal temple housing the relic of the Buddha's tooth; evening puja ceremonies with drumming. Very crowded during the Esala Perahera (July/August).

name: Royal Botanical Gardens Peradeniya
description: Large botanical garden with an orchid house, giant Javan fig tree, palm avenues and river walks.

name: Kandy Lake
description: Artificial lake in the centre of Kandy with a shaded walking path beside the Temple of the Tooth.

name: Udawattakele Forest Reserve
description: Forest reserve right behind Kandy town with trails, birds, monkeys and a small pond.

name: Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue
description: Large white Buddha statue on a hill overlooking Kandy with city views.

name: Kandyan Cultural Dance Show
description: Evening show of traditional Kandyan dancing and drumming, ending with a fire-walking act.

name: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
description: Government-run home for orphaned and injured elephants; visitors watch feeding and river bathing times.

name: Ambuluwawa Tower
description: Spiral tower on a mountain summit with a narrow climb to the top and 360-degree views; symbols of four religions on site.

name: Ramboda Falls
description: Tall multi-tier waterfall on the Kandy-Nuwara Eliya road with a viewing terrace.

name: Gregory Lake
description: Lake in Nuwara Eliya with boat rides, pony rides and lakeside parks; very busy during the April season.

name: Horton Plains and World's End
description: Highland plateau national park with a 9 km loop trail to the World's End cliff drop and Baker's Falls; start early before the mist.

name: Hakgala Botanical Garden
description: Hill-country botanical garden known for its rose garden and ferns below Hakgala rock.

name: Seetha Amman Temple
description: Hindu temple linked to the Ramayana legend of Sita, beside a mountain stream.

name: Pedro Tea Estate
description: Working tea factory with guided tours of tea processing and tea tasting overlooking the plantations.

name: St. Clair's Falls
description: Wide twin waterfall surrounded by tea estates near Talawakele, viewed from a roadside point.

name: Devon Falls
description: Slender high waterfall named after a coffee planter, best seen from the tea centre viewpoint.

name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
description: Sacred mountain with a footprint shrine; pilgrims climb about 5,500 steps overnight to see sunrise. Main season December to May.

name: Nine Arch Bridge
description: Colonial-era stone railway viaduct among jungle and tea; crowds gather to photograph trains crossing.

name: Little Adam's Peak
description: Easy hike through tea fields to a summit with sweeping views of Ella Gap; zipline nearby.

name: Ella Rock
description: Longer, steeper hike from Ella along the railway and through forest to a cliff-top viewpoint.

name: Ravana Falls
description: Roadside waterfall below Ella linked to the Ramayana legend; strongest flow after the rains.

name: Lipton's Seat
description: Viewpoint at the top of the Dambatenne tea estate where Thomas Lipton surveyed his empire; best at sunrise.

name: Dambatenne Tea Factory
description: Historic tea factory built by Lipton in 1890 with tours of the production process.

name: Diyaluma Falls
description: Second-highest waterfall in Sri Lanka; hike to the upper natural rock pools for swimming.

name: Knuckles Mountain Range
description: Rugged forested mountain range with multi-hour treks, villages and high biodiversity. Part of the Central Highlands World Heritage Site.

name: Ella Spice Garden Cooking Class
description: Hands-on Sri Lankan rice and curry cooking classes in Ella using fresh spices and vegetables.

name: Galle Fort
description: Walled 17th-century Dutch fort town with ramparts, lighthouse, boutiques, cafes and colonial streets. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Unawatuna Beach
description: Sheltered crescent bay with calm water for swimming, beach restaurants and snorkelling.

name: Jungle Beach
description: Small cove reached through forest on Rumassala hill, with clear water and coral for snorkelling.

name: Japanese Peace Pagoda
description: White peace stupa on Rumassala hill with views over Galle Fort and the ocean.

name: Hikkaduwa Beach and Coral Sanctuary
description: Lively beach town with a coral reef sanctuary, glass-bottom boats, sea turtles near the shore and a surf break.

name: Kosgoda Turtle Hatchery
description: Conservation hatchery where turtle eggs are protected and hatchlings are released to the sea.

name: Madu River Boat Safari
description: Boat ride through mangrove tunnels and small islands, including a cinnamon island and a temple island.

name: Bentota Beach
description: Long golden beach with jet skiing, banana boats and river water sports where the Bentota river meets the sea.

name: Brief Garden
description: Landscaped garden and home of artist Bevis Bawa, filled with sculptures and quiet garden rooms.

name: Koggala Lake
description: Large lagoon lake with boat trips to small islands, birdlife and a cinnamon island.

name: Stilt Fishermen of Koggala
description: Traditional stilt fishing seen along the shore between Koggala and Weligama, best around sunset.

name: Weligama Beach
description: Wide sandy bay with gentle waves, the most popular place in Sri Lanka for beginner surf lessons.

name: Mirissa Beach
description: Popular palm-lined beach with seafood restaurants, a relaxed vibe and lively evenings.

name: Mirissa Whale Watching
description: Morning boat tours to see blue whales, sperm whales and dolphins off the southern coast. Season is roughly November to April.

name: Coconut Tree Hill
description: Small headland covered in coconut palms overlooking the ocean, one of the most photographed spots on the coast.

name: Dondra Head Lighthouse
description: Tall colonial lighthouse at the southernmost point of Sri Lanka.

name: Paravi Duwa Temple
description: Small island temple off Matara beach connected by a suspension bridge.

name: Hummanaya Blowhole
description: One of the largest blowholes in the world, shooting sea water high into the air; strongest during the southwest monsoon.

name: Mulkirigala Rock Temple
description: Rock temple with five cave terraces of murals and reclining Buddhas, reached by a climb of over 500 steps.

name: Tangalle Beach
description: Long uncrowded beaches and coves, popular for relaxing away from the busier west-coast resorts.

name: Bundala National Park
description: Wetland park and Ramsar site known for migratory birds and flamingos, with crocodiles and elephants.

name: Tissa Wewa
description: Ancient reservoir in Tissamaharama with birdlife and sunset views, a common base for Yala.

name: Yala National Park
description: Sri Lanka's most visited national park, famous for one of the highest leopard densities in the world. Block 1 can get very crowded with jeeps.

name: Kataragama Temple
description: Multi-religious pilgrimage complex sacred to Buddhists, Hindus and Muslims; vibrant evening puja and a large July/August festival.

name: Udawalawe National Park
description: Open grassland park with almost guaranteed sightings of wild elephant herds year-round; elephant transit home nearby.
